text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Panel appointed to study how to improve tertiary education says it has not directed university to charge tuition fees.
- Impressive 1996 profits push up share price of Union Bank of Nigeria while conglomerate PZ Industries slumps because of a glut of its shares on the stock exchange.
- Task force on petroleum products swings into action; summons state oil firm NNPC for talks on Thursday over lingering fuel scarcity in some states.
- A police spokesman reaffirms that opposition group NADECO and its key members are behind recent bomb blasts in Lagos.
- U.S. firm Bechtel pulls out of eight-year-old engineering joint venture with state oil company NNPC, industry sources say.
- Troubled Delta steel company, one of four steel mills in Nigeria, stops production following suspension of budgetary allocation to it by federal authorities.
- Insurance firms will have up till December to raise their capital base to a minimum of 90 million naira from 50 million under a new insurance decree soon to be released, sources say.
- Shell Nigerian unit made a profit of $220 million in 1996, says its chief executive Brian Anderson in an interview with a foreign industry newsletter called Upstream.
- Banks brace up to meet new minimum capital base requirement of 500 million naira from 50 million set for them by the government in a move to purge the sector of the distress syndrome.
